stage1.impression: A moody night view through a shopfront into a warm, hazy bar, and the composition (lightbox, a table lamp at the glass, a deep room) has the right idea. But it reads as CG. The name on the glass is opaque slate-blue extruded letters, not frosting. The glass reflects nothing of the street. A uniform grey veil flattens the whole room. The lightbox is a dull flat panel. The Ember speaker, which should be the hero, is only a faint red smear at the far end that you only find by searching.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker reads at a glance through a clear pane: a saturated red glowing silhouette, lum_median >= 70 and r_median >= 2x g_median in its region
The frosted name reads as acid-etched or frosted glass (translucent, warm-lit from behind, no cool cast, no visible thickness) and not as solid painted letters
The shopfront glass carries faint, believable reflections of the street (the lamps, the kerb) in its upper and lower areas
The room's haze no longer lifts the blacks evenly: shadows behind the glass reach lum_p5 <= 6 while the practicals keep their pools
The pendant lamps are not blown to bare white disks (clip_pct < 5 in the lamp)
The lightbox glows evenly and warmly, with a silhouette that reads as fogged, not as a flat grey card
Resolution and craft at the full 2400 px pass 1:1 checks: no tiling on the fir ceiling, no smeared denoise on the concrete

defects.what: The frosted name renders as opaque, cool blue-grey extruded letters with a visible side face (r70 g77 b85, the only cool colour in a warm frame). It reads as plastic signage, not frosting on the glass.
The Ember speaker barely reads: a thin red line and a dim smear (lum_median 47, r65 g42 b30, nearly the same as the room around it at r61 g41 b28).
The pendant is a blown pure-white disk (clip 33 %, median 204) with no warmth or shape. It reads as a sprite.
No reflections at all on the shopfront glass. Real glass at night from the kerb mirrors the street lamps and the pavement.
Uniform haze veil: the back room's p5 is 23.5 and its range is 70, so everything is milky and low-contrast, like fog in a game.
The lightbox is a dull, cool-pink grey card (median 49) with a hard dark silhouette. It does not glow and reads as a poster.
The fir ceiling shows blocky, repeating patches of texture (tiling) and no checks or nail holes.
The steel fascia over the window has a stuck-on, mottled decal texture across its middle (x 400-500) that reads as a texture seam.
The bottles on the back-bar read as a row of identical, evenly lit white dots (repeated model).
The bottom of the frame (the sill and the kerb) is empty and dark, with no sign of the street or of life outside.

changes.problem: The hero speaker is invisible at a glance: it has the same tone and colour as the room around it.

evidence.measured: lum_median 46.9, r/g/b 65/42/30, against 61/41/28 for the back room [445,190,720,330]

change.setting: on each Ember speaker 4 x area, W/m2 at the target; plus the speaker's lamps and pinholes
change.to: 45 W/m2, 2700 K, with the area lights moved behind and beside the cabinet so light passes through the red acrylic and rims its edges, not only falls on its front

changes.expected: A glowing red silhouette at the end of the room, clearly the only saturated object in the frame

changes.problem: The frosted name reads as solid, cool-blue plastic letters, not frosting, and brings a second colour into the frame.

evidence.measured: median 76, r/g/b 70/77/85 (blue-dominant), hard opaque fill with a side face

change.setting: the window's frosted name: frosted acrylic roughness and emission
change.from: emission 0.03, opaque look, lit cool by the 3000 K street lamps
change.to: a translucent frost (transmission ~0.8, roughness ~0.6, no thickness), emission 0.0, so it is lit warm from the room behind; drop the street lamps to 2700 K

changes.expected: Letters read as a soft, warm-grey translucent veil on the glass, slightly brighter than the room behind them, with b_median no higher than r_median

changes.problem: The haze lifts every shadow evenly, so the room is milky and low in contrast.

change.setting: haze in the room's air: density

changes.expected: Deeper shadows between the pools of light, with the lamps' pools and the speaker standing out. The frame median stays at about 25-32.

changes.problem: The shopfront glass shows no reflections, which is the strongest sign of a render in a through-the-window shot.

evidence.measured: Seen: no mirrored street lamps, pavement or opposite facade anywhere on the glass

change.setting: street lamps and the street behind the camera
change.from: 3 x point, 120 W, 3000 K, nothing behind the camera for the glass to mirror
change.to: Keep the 3 street lamps but put a visible lamp head and a dim facade behind the camera (on the far kerb) so the glass picks up faint (5-10 %) reflections in its upper left and lower right; set the glass's IOR to 1.52 with no anti-reflective tweak

changes.expected: Faint warm reflections layered over the room, mostly in the upper and lower thirds, without hiding the speaker

changes.problem: The pendant's lamp is a blown pure-white disk with no colour.

change.to: 0.6, with the frosted tube emission raised from 0.18 to 0.3 so the fitting reads as a glowing shape

changes.expected: A warm amber pendant with visible form, not clipped

changes.problem: The lightbox reads as a dull grey poster, not a frosted panel glowing from behind.

change.setting: the screens' images emission, and the frosted acrylic's roughness
change.to: 0.9, with the frost roughness raised so the silhouette's edges blur another 2-3x and read as fog

changes.expected: An evenly glowing warm panel (median ~85-110) with a soft, fogged figure. It stays below the hero speaker in saturation.

changes.problem: The fir ceiling and the fascia show tiling and texture patches.

evidence.measured: Seen: blocky repeated patches along the beams, and a mottled decal at x 400-500 on the fascia [0,0,720,50]

change.setting: the stain of the fir and the steel's patina (materials' finish)
change.to: Randomise the UVs per beam (offset and rotation), add procedural checks and darker end grain, and give the steel fascia a continuous, low-contrast brown-black patina without the decal patch

changes.expected: Beams that each read as distinct old timber, and a fascia that reads as one sheet of blackened steel

changes.problem: The kerb side is empty and the back-bar's bottles read as identical copies.

evidence.measured: Seen: a row of identical, evenly lit bottle dots; nothing on the sill or the kerb

change.from: bottles of one model, nothing at the window
change.to: Mix 4-5 bottle shapes and heights on the back-bar; put a half-drunk coupe and a folded menu on the window table and a coat over the near chair

changes.expected: The room reads as lived in and the back-bar as real stock

out_of_scope.request: Place the Ember pair nearer the window or make it larger in the frame
out_of_scope.why: The layout is fixed. Use light (c1) or a longer lens/camera move, not a change to the room.

out_of_scope.request: Remove the dimensional depth of the letters if they are modelled as extruded solids
out_of_scope.why: The shopfront's design is fixed. If the name is modelled as thick letters, changing it is a design question for the owner, not a finish fix.
